subject: Vendor onboarding: certifying tax classification and signing authority for PO issuance
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@lumenlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumen Labs Finance <ap@lumenlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: New vendor onboarding - tax form and signer for PO #56821

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick onboarding window. Per our intake form, we've attached Lumen Labs' completed W-9 (PDF) and a draft authorization letter that names our AP manager as an authorized signer for vendor agreements and PO acceptance. Please confirm if the W-9 is sufficient for you to create the vendor record and issue PO #56821.

Attachments: Lumen_W9_20250513.pdf, authorization_letter_lumen_signed.pdf

A couple of notes: our legal name on the W-9 is "Lumen Labs, Inc." but our banking remit comes from "Lumen Labs Finance" (same EIN). If you need a separate remit agreement or ACH form, let me know and I can route it.

Best,
Elena
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Lumen Labs

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@lumenlabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding - tax form and signer for PO #56821

Elena —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear note on remit. Quick checklist from procurement to get PO 56821 into the system:

- Confirm tax ID (EIN) on W-9 matches our EIN verification lookup.
- Confirm the signing authority on the authorization letter is acceptable (name + title + organization stamp preferred).
- Confirm whether Lumen prefers a single consolidated PO to the corporate EIN (recommended) or multiple POs per remit name.

I ran the EIN against our lookup tool and got a partial match: the name on file is "Lumen Labs Incorporated" (suffix differs). That triggers a quick KYC step — we need either a screenshot of the IRS EIN match page, a certified letter, or a secondary ID (e.g., incorporation certificate) so we can clear the vendor without putting the PO on hold.

Kimberly — can you advise whether the signed authorization letter in the current form is acceptable for signature delegation? If not, can procurement accept a DocuSign envelope with the AP manager as signer?

Elena, if you can provide any of the items above it will speed things up. If not, we can approach finance for a limited-release PO with conditional payment terms.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@lumenlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding - tax form and signer for PO #56821

Soojin / Elena —

Thanks for the context. A few operational points:

- The authorization letter as submitted is OK provided it contains the printed name, title, and either a corporate seal or a link to a signed DocuSign envelope that we can verify.
- For the EIN/name mismatch: procurement policy requires a corroborating document when the vendor name differs by more than punctuation/abbreviation. "Lumen Labs, Inc." vs "Lumen Labs Incorporated" is not purely stylistic in our system, so please provide one of the following:
  * IRS EIN confirmation screenshot (preferred), or
  * Certificate of incorporation naming the legal entity, or
  * A W-9 with the exact legal entity name matching the IRS record.

If Lumen can send a DocuSign envelope where AP signs the authorization letter and we receive the audit trail URL, that will satisfy both signer verification and document integrity.

Operational workaround: we can provision PO 56821 into the system but mark payments on hold until EIN verification clears. That allows your engineers to start onboarding for delivery tracking while finance retains control of disbursements.

Marissa — please prepare the PO in the system as "Pending Payment Authorization" and tag it with hold code: TAX_NAME_MISMATCH. I'll escalate to finance if this blocks critical runway.

Kimberly
Sr. Accounts Payable Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@lumenlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumen Labs Finance <ap@lumenlabs.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding - tax form and signer for PO #56821

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is an IRS EIN confirmation screenshot and a DocuSign audit link for the authorization letter. The DocuSign envelope shows Maria Gonzales (AP Manager) signed on 2025-05-19; envelope ID: ABC123LUMEN (link below).

Per Kimberly's note, we are happy to have PO 56821 issued as "Pending Payment Authorization" so work can begin while payments remain on hold until finance completes their checks. Please confirm final PO number once created.

Attachments: Lumen_W9_20250513.pdf, authorization_letter_lumen_signed.pdf
Related DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/recipient/view?envelopeId=ABC123LUMEN

Appreciate it — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Elena
